# Katelynn Alexander

> Independent consultant specializing in AWS cost optimization, legacy system modernization, and zero-downtime release engineering (DevOps advisory), with 10+ years building production systems at Nike.

Katelynn Alexander is an independent software consultant currently taking on new consulting engagements. She spent 10+ years as a software engineer and engineering manager at Nike, most recently leading engineering for critical financial integration systems, before going independent. Every engagement starts with an assessment and a plan; hands-on implementation is available as an optional add-on for teams that want it executed rather than handed off.

## Service: AWS Cost Optimization Audit & Remediation

Audits AWS environments to find and quantify wasted cloud spend, then delivers a prioritized remediation plan. Covers right-sizing EC2/Lambda, decommissioning unused managed services, moving databases to on-demand pricing, and removing unneeded "just in case" infrastructure. Standard deliverable is the audit and plan; hands-on implementation is an optional add-on. Documented track record: 60–70% reduction in AWS infrastructure spend on a production system, $2,000+/month in recurring savings identified and implemented on a single service line, zero-downtime remediation execution.

Q: How much can I expect to save on my AWS bill?
A: It depends on how much drift has accumulated, but 30–70% reductions are common in systems that haven't had a dedicated cost review in over a year. Savings are quantified in the audit before any implementation decision is made.

Q: Do you implement the changes, or just deliver a report?
A: The standard engagement is the audit and remediation plan. Hands-on implementation is a separate, higher-cost add-on.

Q: Will implementation require downtime?
A: No. Remediation plans are designed for zero-downtime execution against live production systems.

## Service: Legacy System Modernization

Assesses legacy backend systems (outdated frameworks, brittle integration layers, deprecated authentication) and delivers a sequenced modernization roadmap without disrupting dependent systems. Covers replacing legacy integration layers, upgrading unsupported language/framework versions, and modernizing authentication/security patterns. Standard deliverable is the assessment and roadmap; hands-on execution is an optional add-on. Applies to any industry, not just finance. Proof points: multiple large-scale legacy integration replacements delivered with no production incidents, framework/language/authentication modernization delivered across systems processing global transaction volume, critical CVE remediation executed on production systems under compliance requirements.

Q: How do you modernize a system without breaking production?
A: Through an incremental, sequenced plan: parallel-running old and new systems where needed, validating against real production behavior before cutover, and always defining a rollback path first.

Q: What if the system has no documentation?
A: That's the typical starting condition. The assessment phase includes reverse-engineering actual system behavior and dependencies.

Q: Do you only work with financial systems?
A: No. Deep experience in compliance-heavy financial systems, but the approach applies to any critical legacy system.

## Service: Zero-Downtime Release Advisory

Helps teams build toward zero-downtime releases: feature flags that decouple deploying from releasing, dark deployment pipelines validated against real production traffic, and resilient architecture patterns (circuit breakers, graceful degradation, rollback-by-default). Phased engagement starting with a readiness assessment, sequenced by lowest-effort/highest-impact first, not a full rebuild. Standard deliverable is the assessment and phased roadmap; hands-on implementation and cutover support are optional add-ons. Proof point: zero-incident production cutovers delivered across multiple markets and regions, including during peak-traffic periods.

Q: Can this work for a team with brittle, tightly-coupled legacy architecture?
A: Yes, that's the typical starting point, not an edge case.

Q: Does this require a full architecture rebuild?
A: No. The roadmap starts with the highest-impact, lowest-effort changes first.

Q: What's the difference between this and general DevOps consulting?
A: This is specifically about de-risking the moment of release (feature flags, dark deployments, rollback design), not general CI/CD or infrastructure management.

Also open to fractional/advisory engagements outside these three named services.
